answers.value: All engineering squads in the value stream that closed a sprint in the period; one retrospective per squad per sprint, tracked as Jira issue type 'Retrospective' under the team's board.
The two-week sprint just closed (sprint end date minus 13 calendar days through sprint end date); retro held within 3 business days of sprint close.

Each retro record must have: sprint id, attendee list, at least 3 'what went well' items, at least 3 'what to improve' items, and >=1 action item with an owner and due date; Confluence retro page linked from the Jira retro issue.
Count of retros held = count of squads with a closed sprint in the period; reconcile the Jira retro-issue count against the sprint-report count with 0 variance.
Confluence retro page version timestamp plus the Jira retro issue transition-to-Done timestamp retained for 24 months in the team space.
Any squad that skipped a retro is logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with reason and a make-up date within 5 business days; owner = Scrum Master.
All sprint retrospectives held in the reporting quarter across the value stream's squads (typically 20-30 retro records).
Pass = 100% of closed sprints have a linked retro record with >=1 owned action item; fail if <100%. Action-item carryover into the next sprint must be >=70% closed.
Missing or incomplete retro raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' assigned to the Scrum Master with a 5-business-day remediation SLA.
Jira fields: Sprint (sprint id), Issue Type = Retrospective, Assignee (facilitator), Linked Confluence page URL; Confluence retro template columns Went Well / Improve / Action / Owner / Due.
Sprint-report squad count for the period sourced from Jira; used as the control total against retro-issue count.

Acceptance: every closed sprint has a completed retro (Jira type 'Retrospective', status Done) with a linked, versioned Confluence retro page containing owned, dated action items. Evidence stored in the team Confluence space and the Jira board; retro dashboard filter saved as 'Retro Compliance - <squad>'.

checklist.step: Run the sprint retrospective as a scheduled knowledge-sharing session
checklist.value: Retro on the calendar recurring per sprint; facilitator = Scrum Master; notes captured in Confluence team space.

testing.step: Verify a knowledge-sharing session occurred for the sprint
testing.value: Confluence retro page exists with a version timestamp inside the sprint window and an attendee list.

checklist.step: Capture significant decisions from the retro as ADRs

testing.step: Confirm retro-driven decisions were recorded as ADRs
testing.value: For each retro action tagged 'decision', a matching ADR file exists in /docs/adr referenced from the retro page.

checklist.step: Record retro action items and outcomes in a maintained changelog/log
checklist.value: Retro action items tracked in Jira with status; carryover items visible on the next sprint board.

testing.value: Every retro action item has a Jira status not older than one sprint without an update.

answers.value: Knowledge outputs produced from every sprint retrospective in the period: lessons learned, action items, and reusable engineering guidance, published to the team Confluence space and cross-linked from the Jira retro issue.
The sprint just closed; outputs recorded within 3 business days of the retro.
Each output record must have: source sprint id, category (lesson/action/pattern), owner, and a Confluence page URL; action items must have a due date and Jira link.
Number of published knowledge pages = number of retros held in the period; reconcile Confluence page count to Jira retro-issue count with 0 variance.
Confluence page version + last-modified timestamp retained 24 months; export saved to the team space page tree under 'Retrospective Outputs'.
Any retro with no captured output logged as Jira 'SDLC-Exception', owner = Scrum Master, 5-business-day remediation SLA.
All retrospective knowledge pages published in the reporting quarter across the value stream's squads.
Pass = 100% of retros have a linked, categorized Confluence output page with owned action items; fail if <100%.
Missing output page raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' assigned to the Scrum Master with a 5-business-day remediation SLA.
Confluence 'Retrospective Outputs' template fields: Source Sprint, Category, Description, Owner, Linked Jira, Due Date; page labelled 'retro-output'.
Jira retro-issue count for the period used as the control total against the count of 'retro-output'-labelled Confluence pages.

Acceptance: each retrospective yields a published, labelled ('retro-output') Confluence page categorizing lessons, patterns, and owned/dated action items, cross-linked to the Jira retro issue. Evidence stored in the Confluence 'Retrospective Outputs' tree.

checklist.step: Keep captured knowledge outputs current in Confluence
checklist.value: Retro output pages reviewed and updated each sprint; stale pages (>90 days untouched with open actions) flagged.

testing.value: No 'retro-output' page has an open action item and a last-modified date older than one sprint.

checklist.step: Feed captured outputs back into knowledge-sharing sessions
checklist.value: Top lessons from the period's retro outputs presented in a weekly engineering knowledge-sharing session, with slides in Confluence.

testing.step: Confirm outputs surfaced in a sharing session
testing.value: A weekly session agenda in Confluence references at least one retro output page from the period.

checklist.step: Promote durable decisions in outputs to ADRs
checklist.value: Any decision-class output recorded as an ADR in /docs/adr and linked from the output page.

testing.value: Each output tagged 'decision' has a corresponding ADR file referenced by URL.

answers.value: All implementation-governance decisions and design-assurance gate outcomes for changes deployed in the reporting period across the value stream; each gate outcome recorded in the GRC platform as a governance record linked to its change ticket.
The reporting quarter (calendar quarter just ended); leadership report delivered within 10 business days of quarter close.
Each governance record must have: change ticket id, gate name, outcome (pass/conditional/fail), reviewer, date, and remediation status; open exceptions must carry a due date and owner.
Number of governance records in the report = number of deployed changes requiring a gate in the period; reconcile GRC record count to the change-ticket count with 0 variance.
Report PDF plus underlying GRC export retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository, versioned with quarter tag (e.g. 'GovReport-2026Q2-v1').
Any gate failure or unremediated finding logged as a GRC issue with disposition (accepted/remediating/waived); owner = Enterprise Architect; waivers require ARB approval.
Prior-quarter governance metrics compared against current quarter (gate pass rate, mean remediation days); variance and trend explained in the report narrative.
Each governance record links to its ServiceNow/Jira change ticket id; unlinked records are a reconciliation defect and must be resolved before the report is finalized.
All governance gate outcomes recorded in the GRC platform for the reporting quarter.
Pass = report reconciles 100% to GRC records and every finding has a disposition; fail if any record lacks an outcome, reviewer, or disposition.
Discrepancy between report and GRC data raises a GRC issue assigned to the Enterprise Architect with a 5-business-day remediation SLA before sign-off.
Delegation matrix in the GRC platform maps each gate to its approving authority (ARB chair, Enterprise Architect, CISO for security gates) with named backups; reviewed quarterly.

Acceptance: governance report reconciles 1:1 to GRC gate records for the quarter, every finding carries a disposition and owner, and prior-quarter comparison is included. Evidence: versioned report PDF + GRC export in the compliance evidence repository.

checklist.step: Report on ARB approval status of major initiatives
checklist.value: Report includes a section listing each major initiative and its ARB approval/exception status sourced from GRC.

testing.step: Verify every major initiative has an ARB decision recorded
testing.value: Cross-check: no in-scope major initiative in GRC lacks an ARB approval or documented exception.

checklist.step: Report deployments blocked by failed governance gates
checklist.value: Report shows count of deployments blocked by gate failures and their remediation state.

testing.value: For each 'fail' gate outcome, the linked change ticket shows deployment held until remediation or waiver.

checklist.step: Track each governed item's status through its lifecycle in the report
checklist.value: Each governance record shows a lifecycle status (proposed/approved/implemented/closed) in the report tables.

testing.value: No governance record in the reporting set has a null or stale lifecycle status.

checklist.step: Report CI/CD quality-gate pass/fail outcomes feeding governance
checklist.value: Report aggregates SonarQube/pipeline quality-gate results per release as an input metric to governance.

testing.step: Verify quality-gate metrics tie to pipeline data
testing.value: Reported quality-gate pass rate matches the pipeline system's recorded gate results for the period.

checklist.step: Confirm SDLC/design-assurance governance controls were exercised
checklist.value: Governance report evidences secure-SDLC gates (design review, code review, security testing) applied to each in-scope change.

testing.step: Verify SDLC gate evidence exists per change
testing.value: Sample 10% of changes; each has GRC evidence of design-assurance gate completion prior to production.

answers.value: All functional and non-functional requirements for the feature/epic being built, elicited from the Product Owner and named SMEs; captured as Jira stories under the epic with acceptance criteria.
The elaboration window for the current program increment / sprint intake; requirements agreed before the story enters 'Ready for Dev'.
Every story must have: a user-story statement, testable acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then), Product Owner sign-off, and links to any SME source docs in Confluence.
Count of agreed stories = count of scoped requirements from the intake list; reconcile Jira story count to the requirements register with 0 unmapped items.
Confluence requirements page version timestamp + Jira story history retained for the project lifetime + 24 months in the team space.

Ambiguous or contested requirements logged as Jira 'Clarification' sub-tasks with owner and due date; unresolved items block 'Ready for Dev' and are raised as 'SDLC-Exception' if aging >5 business days.
All stories in the epic intended for the upcoming sprint(s).
Pass = 100% of stories entering the sprint have PO-approved, testable acceptance criteria; fail if any story lacks acceptance criteria or PO sign-off.
Requirement gaps found during dev raise a Jira 'Clarification' assigned to the Business Analyst; if unresolved in 5 business days, escalate as 'SDLC-Exception' to the Product Owner.
Jira story fields: Summary, Description (user story), Acceptance Criteria (custom field), Epic Link, Linked Confluence requirement page; INVEST criteria applied at refinement.
Requirements register (Confluence table) row count for the epic used as the control total against Jira story count.

Authorized approver = Product Owner (owner of backlog acceptance); delegation matrix in Confluence names the Product Owner as primary and the Business Analyst as backup for requirement sign-off, reviewed each PI.

checklist.step: Attach testable acceptance criteria to every requirement
checklist.value: Each Jira story carries Given/When/Then acceptance criteria agreed with the Product Owner.

testing.step: Verify acceptance criteria present and testable
testing.value: Sample all sprint-bound stories; 100% have non-empty, verifiable acceptance criteria.

checklist.step: Document assumptions and constraints surfaced during elicitation
checklist.value: Assumptions/constraints captured in the Confluence requirements page and linked from the epic.

testing.value: Requirements page has a populated Assumptions and Constraints section reviewed by the Product Owner.

checklist.step: Peer-review the requirements before development starts
checklist.value: Requirements reviewed by Tech Lead and Business Analyst; review comments resolved on the Confluence page.

testing.value: Confluence page shows reviewer sign-off and resolved comments dated before 'Ready for Dev'.

answers.value: The set of stories proposed for the upcoming sprint plus the squad's capacity for that sprint; validated in Jira against team velocity and member availability.
The upcoming two-week sprint; feasibility confirmed during sprint planning before commitment is locked.
Each candidate story must have story points estimated, no unresolved blockers, and a defined acceptance criterion; team capacity must account for PTO, ceremonies, and support load.
Committed story points must be <= rolling 3-sprint average velocity; reconcile committed points against capacity-adjusted velocity with the delta shown in the sprint planning notes.
Sprint planning Confluence note (capacity, velocity, commitment) versioned and timestamped; retained 24 months in the team space and linked from the sprint in Jira.
Over-commitment (committed points > 110% of capacity-adjusted velocity) logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with justification; owner = Scrum Master; requires Product Owner acknowledgement.
All stories proposed for the upcoming sprint (the planning candidate set).
Pass = committed points within 90-110% of capacity-adjusted velocity and 100% of committed stories estimated and blocker-free; fail otherwise.
Infeasible commitment triggers descope negotiation with the Product Owner; residual over-commitment logged as 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Scrum Master with a same-sprint resolution SLA.
The upcoming sprint's start and end dates as defined in Jira; capacity computed for exactly those working days.

checklist.step: Compute squad capacity before committing the sprint
checklist.value: Capacity = team member days minus PTO, ceremonies, and support allocation, recorded in the sprint planning note.

testing.step: Verify capacity was calculated and applied
testing.value: Sprint planning note shows a numeric capacity figure and committed points do not exceed it beyond the 110% threshold.

checklist.step: Validate commitment against capacity and velocity
checklist.value: Committed points compared to rolling 3-sprint velocity; validation result noted in the sprint.

testing.value: Planning note records velocity, capacity, and the go/no-go decision with the Scrum Master's sign-off.

checklist.step: Identify dependencies for each candidate story
checklist.value: Each candidate story has its blocking dependencies linked in Jira before it is committed.

testing.value: No committed story has an unlinked known dependency; dependency links present on the board.

answers.value: Developer experience metrics for the reporting quarter across all engineering squads: DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR), PR cycle time, build success rate, and developer-survey scores; sourced into the enterprise data warehouse.
The reporting quarter (calendar quarter just ended); report delivered to leadership within 10 business days of quarter close.
Every metric must have: a definition, source system, calculation window, unit, and target/benchmark; DORA metrics computed per the standard four-key definitions with no nulls in the reporting rows.
Metric row counts in the BI report reconcile to source-system extracts (pipeline, Jira, survey tool) with variance <= 1%; totals footed against the warehouse fact tables.
Report snapshot (BI export + query definitions) versioned with quarter tag and retained 24 months in the reporting repository; data lineage captured in the data catalog.
Any metric with a data-quality gap or missing source is footnoted and logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception'; owner = Data Engineer; 10-business-day remediation SLA.
All developer-experience metric records for the reporting quarter across squads.
Pass = report reconciles to source extracts within 1% and every metric has a definition and target; fail if any headline metric is unreconciled or undefined.
Reconciliation break raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' assigned to the Data Engineer with a 5-business-day remediation SLA before the report is released.
Delegation matrix in the reporting repository names the Tech Lead as report approver and the Data Engineer as data-owner backup; reviewed quarterly.
The reporting quarter's exact start and end dates; all metrics computed over that window and stated in the report header.

checklist.step: Include RED/DORA delivery metrics in the report
checklist.value: Deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, and MTTR computed and charted per squad.

testing.value: Reported DORA values reconcile to pipeline and incident-system data for the quarter.

checklist.step: Ensure completeness of the metric dataset
checklist.value: Reporting rows are >=99% complete across required metric fields before publication.

testing.value: Data-quality check shows null rate <1% on required metric columns; failures block release.

checklist.step: Publish the developer-experience quality/health scores
checklist.value: Scores published to the BI dashboard and shared with engineering leadership each quarter.

testing.value: Dashboard shows the current-quarter scores with the publish timestamp.

answers.value: The release candidate's completed scope: all stories in the release meeting the Definition of Done, requiring Product Owner acceptance sign-off before the RC tag is cut.
The release window for the current increment; sign-off recorded before the release branch/tag is cut.
Every RC story must show acceptance criteria met, UAT/demo evidence linked, and no open blocker defects; sign-off record must name the approver, date, and RC version.
Count of accepted stories = count of stories in the release scope; reconcile Jira 'Accepted' stories to the release scope list with 0 unaccepted in-scope items.
Sign-off recorded as a Jira transition + Confluence release-acceptance page, versioned with the RC tag, retained 24 months in the release space.
Any story accepted with a known limitation logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with disposition and a follow-up ticket; owner = Product Owner.
Acceptance decision documented on the Confluence release-acceptance page: approver, date, RC version, scope accepted, and any conditions; linked from the Jira release.
Sign-off notification sent to Release Manager, Tech Lead, and QA Lead via the release Jira issue watchers and the #release channel; recipients recorded on the acceptance page.
All stories in the release-candidate scope.
Pass = Product Owner acceptance recorded for 100% of in-scope stories with no open blocker defects; fail if any in-scope story is unaccepted or a blocker is open.
Missing sign-off blocks the RC cut; a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' is raised to the Product Owner with a same-day remediation SLA before release proceeds.
Delegation matrix in the release space names the Product Owner as acceptance authority and a designated proxy PO as backup; RC cut authority held by the Release Manager, reviewed each release.
The release window's dates; the acceptance sign-off is valid only for the RC version cut within that window and is re-taken if scope changes.

checklist.step: Record Product Owner acceptance of each story
checklist.value: Each in-scope story transitioned to 'Accepted' in Jira by the Product Owner with a comment referencing evidence.

testing.value: All in-scope stories show status 'Accepted' with the Product Owner as the transitioning user before the RC tag.

checklist.step: Capture formal deliverable acceptance for the release
checklist.value: Confluence release-acceptance page signed by the Product Owner with RC version and conditions.

testing.value: Acceptance page has a dated Product Owner sign-off matching the RC version.

checklist.step: Ensure UAT sign-off precedes acceptance
checklist.value: UAT results linked from the acceptance page; no failed UAT case open at sign-off.

testing.value: UAT summary shows pass with sign-off dated before the acceptance record.

answers.value: Real-time ingestion jobs for the in-scope streaming sources (e.g. policy/claims/billing event topics on Kafka); each job reads a named source topic and lands raw records to the Bronze/landing layer of the lakehouse.
The build sprint for the streaming pipeline; job considered done when it runs continuously against source topics in the non-prod environment for >=24 hours without unhandled failures.

Ingestion job config must specify: source topic/connection, schema (registered in the schema registry), checkpoint/offset store, dead-letter topic, and idempotency key; all required config keys present and validated in CI.
Records consumed from the source topic reconcile to records landed in Bronze within the watermark window; consumer-lag and landed-count delta <= 0.1% over a 24-hour soak.
Job manifest, schema version, and soak-test run logs committed to the repo and retained with the build artifact; pipeline run id and timestamp recorded in the CI/CD system.

Malformed or unprocessable records routed to a dead-letter topic and logged; any sustained lag or DLQ growth raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Data Engineer with a 5-business-day remediation SLA.

checklist.step: Use change-data-capture / streaming ingestion for real-time sources
checklist.value: Ingestion implemented as a streaming consumer (Kafka/CDC) rather than batch polling; connector config in the repo.

testing.value: Source event appears in Bronze within the SLA latency window during the soak test.

checklist.step: Make ingestion idempotent
checklist.value: Idempotency/dedup key configured so replays do not duplicate landed records.

testing.value: Replaying an offset range produces no net new duplicate rows in Bronze (count unchanged).

checklist.step: Handle schema evolution on the stream
checklist.value: Consumer bound to the schema registry with a compatibility mode (backward) so evolving schemas do not break ingestion.

testing.value: A backward-compatible schema change is ingested without job failure; incompatible change is rejected to DLQ.

checklist.step: Add monitoring and alerting on the ingestion job
checklist.value: Consumer lag, throughput, and DLQ depth exported to metrics with alerts on threshold breach.

testing.value: Injected lag/DLQ growth triggers an alert to the on-call channel during test.

answers.value: Real-time transformation jobs applied to ingested streams: cleansing, enrichment, and business-rule transforms that read Bronze/landing records and produce Silver/curated output topics or tables in the lakehouse.
The build sprint for the streaming transforms; job done when it produces validated output continuously against ingested streams for >=24 hours in non-prod.

Transform config must specify: input Bronze source, output schema, windowing/watermark strategy, data-quality rules, and error/DLQ handling; all required transform parameters present and validated in CI.
Input record count reconciles to output + filtered + DLQ counts (conservation of records) within 0.1% over a 24-hour soak; row-level checksums sampled for enrichment accuracy.
Transform code, unit/integration test results, and soak-test lineage committed to the repo and retained with the artifact; run id and timestamp in the CI/CD system.
Records failing DQ rules routed to a quarantine/DLQ table with reason codes; recurring failures raise a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Data Engineer with a 5-business-day remediation SLA.

checklist.step: Make the transformation idempotent
checklist.value: Stateful transforms keyed with checkpointing so reprocessing yields identical output; exactly-once or effectively-once semantics configured.

testing.value: Reprocessing the same input window produces byte-identical output rows (no duplicates or drift).

checklist.step: Land transformed output in the Silver/Gold medallion layer
checklist.value: Transform writes curated records to the Silver layer following the Bronze/Silver/Gold convention.

testing.value: Output tables are registered in the Silver layer with the expected curated schema.

checklist.step: Apply data validation within the transform
checklist.value: DQ rules (type, range, referential) enforced on the stream; invalid records quarantined.

testing.value: Injected invalid records are routed to quarantine with reason codes; valid records pass through.

checklist.step: Add integration tests for the transform against upstream/downstream
checklist.value: Integration tests run in CI against a Bronze fixture and assert Silver output shape and values.

testing.step: Verify integration tests pass in CI
testing.value: CI pipeline shows the transform's integration test suite green on the merge commit.

answers.value: All blocking dependencies identified on backlog items proposed for the upcoming sprint; each blocker tracked as a Jira issue link ('is blocked by') on its story.
The refinement-to-planning window for the upcoming sprint; blockers cleared before items enter the sprint commitment.
Each blocker must have: a linked blocking issue, an owner, a target resolution date, and a status; a story is 'Ready' only when all its blocking links are resolved or explicitly waived.
Count of open blockers on sprint-candidate stories must reach 0 (or documented waiver) before commitment; reconcile the Jira blocker-link report to the candidate story list.
Blocker resolution history retained in Jira issue links + comments; a dependency-status snapshot saved to the sprint planning Confluence note, versioned and timestamped.
Unresolved blockers at planning logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with owner and escalation; the blocked story is descoped or the blocker escalated to the Scrum Master with a same-sprint SLA.
All stories proposed for the upcoming sprint that carry one or more 'is blocked by' links.
Pass = 0 open blockers (or all waived with justification) on committed stories; fail if any committed story has an unresolved blocking link.
A blocker that cannot be cleared before planning triggers descope or escalation as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Scrum Master with a same-sprint remediation SLA.
Acceptance: every sprint-candidate story has zero unresolved blocking dependencies at commitment, evidenced by the Jira blocker-link report showing all links resolved or waived.
Evidence: Jira blocker-link report filter 'Sprint Candidates - Open Blockers' plus the dependency snapshot on the sprint planning Confluence note.

checklist.step: Identify and link all dependencies before sprint entry
checklist.value: Every candidate story has its blocking dependencies linked in Jira with owners.

testing.value: Jira report shows no committed story with an unlinked known dependency.

checklist.step: Track cross-team dependencies to resolution
checklist.value: Cross-team blockers raised on the program board with the owning team and target date.
